newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electric futures settle up with physicals.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electric futures settle up with physicals.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures finished Friday sharply higher on another rally in spot natural gas prices and the outlook for colder-than-normal weather in the Pacific Northwest.
"It's just a strong market physically," said a Northwest futures trader, referring to the strength in the underlying western power market behind the rise the past couple of sessions.
December physical power deliveries at the California-Oregon Border (COB) were quoted at $25.00-$25.40 a megawatt hour (MWh) and at the Palo Verde (PV) switchyard in Arizona at $23.25-$23.45.
Western natgas prices rose in lock step with their Gulf Coast counterpart, with Canadian values at the AECO storage hub in Alberta hitting year-highs around C$2 per gigajoule, market sources said.
December natural gas delivered to the San Juan/Blanco Hub was assessed in the high-$2.50 to low-$2.60 per million thermal units, up from Thursday's $2.49-$2.53 range.
December COB futures settled up 67 cents at $25.50 a megawatt hour after it touched $25.95, near its life-of-contract high at $26.00.
Most traders agreed that there would be strong resistance at that $26 level.
January COB finished up 77 cents at $23.02 but lower than its session high of $23.50. Deferred COB months ended steady to 75 cents higher.
December PV futures settled at $23.59, up 59 cents after briefly hitting $23.90 in late trading.
January PV finished at $21.00, up 75 cents. Outer PV contracts ended an average of 25 cents higher.
NYMEX said an estimated 119 COB and 93 PV contracts traded.
Temperatures in the Northwest are expected to dip to slightly below-normal levels this weekend through Monday and then fall to as low as 20 degrees Fahrenheit below-normal on Tuesday.
In the Southwest, forecasters are calling for normal to slightly above-normal temperatures through next week.
